summary: An excerpt from a fiction novel (Book 14, part 73) in which a narrator questions a lawyer-like woman about the legality of recording conversations, lying to federal officials, and the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act, while she probes what the narrator plans to do to help a brother named Wilson facing FBI entrapment. The narrator hypothetically describes a sting plan to expose FBI entrapment tactics by staging a recording and documentary. The passage is dialogue-driven and mixes legal discussion with banter.
one_line: Fictional excerpt where Zenobia questions a lawyer about recording police, lying to federal officials, and a plan to expose FBI entrapment.
key_facts: In Minnesota, it is legal to record conversations so long as at least one of the parties consents.
Recording conversations with police or federal officers is legal, though officers may not like it and may arrest the recorder on some other pretext.
There is a law against making false statements to federal officials, but cops can lie unless under oath.
The lawyer warns the narrator to constrain answers to a yes or no regarding awareness of the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act and its penalties.
The narrator says Wilson was entrapped by the FBI into saying he would do things he never would have done otherwise.
The narrator's hypothetical plan is to pick someone who deserved jail for a different reason and have an actor record him saying radical things.
In the hypothetical plan, the actor would take the recording to the FBI and offer to be an informant.
The hypothetical plan includes having a famous filmmaker with a billion Twitter followers make a documentary exposing FBI tactics.
The lawyer asks to keep the discussion in the realm of hypotheticals so she would not have to reveal plans if questioned under oath.
The narrator's sister Zenobia is told she needs to take care because her brother has enough problems.
The lawyer has a killer glare and the narrator says they would not want to face her in a courtroom.
